notes: DEFECT REPRODUCED AND FIXED, at 0 vendor runs. Upstream apicula PR #535's case is a bank holding a true-LVDS output pair and ordinary single-ended IBUFs: `BankDesc` records the pair's bank-wide `IO_TYPE` as LVDS, and `Device.process_IBUF` applied that bank-wide type to every plain IBUF unconditionally, so each single-ended input in the bank was packed as LVDS. The port is behavioural, not textual: an IBUF now adopts the bank-wide standard only when the bank has an ordinary (non-LVDS) output, and an input-only bank leaves each IBUF on its own `IO_TYPE` or the device default. 138C inherits `Device.process_IBUF`/`check_io_banks` unmodified and `GW5A_25A` keeps its own separate override untouched, so the fix reaches this die without touching a frozen 25A path. MEASURED HOW: the mixed-bank tests fail against the pre-fix `process_IBUF` and pass against the fixed one, against a stubbed chipdb -- fail-then-pass, not assertion-free; a guard pins the single-type bank's `IO_TYPE` fuse as unchanged; a negative test confirms an explicit per-pin `IO_TYPE` conflict is still refused by name (`BankDesc.check_or_set_attr`), so the relaxation did not become permissiveness. `apicula tests/test_bank_coercion_138c.py` (6 tests, all pass). NOT MEASURED, and named rather than implied: no bitstream on this board exercises the case. The die's only `TRUELVDS` pair is `J14`/`H14` (`IOR103A`/`B`) and no design in this phase's corpus places a single-ended IBUF in that pair's bank, so there is no vendor bitstream to diff and the row closes at `E0` on the packer, not on the bitstream. The bitstream-level point is one vendor run on a bank plan that mixes the two, and it is the Hardware Gate's to spend if it wants it.
